title: Split shell_check.sh (428 lines) into an entry script and three libs
objective: Bring linux_configuration/scripts/meta/shell_check.sh under the repo-wide 250-line cap by moving its install, discovery and linting functions into lib/shell_check_{install,discover,lint}.sh, without changing which files it discovers or which linters it runs.
acceptance_criteria: shell_check.sh and each new lib/shell_check_*.sh file is at most 250 lines.
shellcheck reports zero findings across the entry script and all three libs, at the repo's no-severity-filter setting, with no suppression added.
The set of functions defined across the entry and the libs is identical to the nine defined at HEAD, each defined exactly once.
Every executable line of the original survives; the only additions are the three source lines.
Running the script with --skip-install --list-only --verbose discovers exactly the same file list as the same invocation at HEAD, plus the three new lib files themselves and nothing else.
No lib sources another lib; the entry sources all three, after the option parsing and the temp-file paths they read.
The entry keeps the mktemp -d and its EXIT trap, so cleanup still happens on every exit path.
out_of_scope: Running the script without --list-only. Its install_linters path invokes sudo pacman and an AUR helper, and --skip-install does not gate the AUR branch; decision 6 forbids mutating the live system.
Fixing the --skip-install flag so it also suppresses the AUR install path. That is a real defect but a behaviour change, not a line-count split.
Changing the 2-space indentation this file uses, which differs from the tab-indented scripts elsewhere in the repo.
verifier: shellcheck over the entry plus all three libs (expects zero findings), bash -n on each, bash ~/utils/scripts/check_file_length.sh over the four files (expects none listed), a diff of the --list-only --verbose file list against the same run from a detached worktree at HEAD (expects only the three new libs added), a function-set diff against HEAD (expects identical), and a sorted line-set diff (expects only the three source lines added).
